chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'shah) from An-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the male and female slave who are manumitted upon the master's death (tadbir). He said: 'It is for his master to manumipate them by writing a deed of manumission (mukatabah) if he wishes, and it is not for him to sell them unless the slave wishes to sell himself for the duration of his life, and it is for him to take their wealth if they have wealth.'

key_terms.قَدْرَ حَيَاتِهِ: For the duration of his life
key_terms.يُكَاتِبَهُ: To enter into a contract of manumission (Mukatabah)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of an owner regarding a slave designated for manumission upon death (tadbir)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific legal status of a *dabir* (slave manumitted upon the owner's death), emphasizing that the owner retains the right to initiate *mukatabah* (contract of manumission) rather than being forced to grant immediate freedom. The ruling highlights the owner's limited power to sell the slave—only with the slave's consent for their remaining lifespan—while affirming the owner's entitlement to the slave's accumulated wealth, reflecting the nuanced balance between the slave's path to liberty and the owner's property rights in Shia jurisprudence.
